concepts.title: Cash and Cash Equivalents
concepts.definition: For this statement, cash means cash in hand and demand deposits, while cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid placements -- typically marketable securities and bank or short-term deposits falling due within about three months -- that can be converted into known amounts of cash without material risk.
concepts.key_idea: Bank overdraft, cash credit and short-term deposits sit with the equivalents, so movements inside this family are not cash flows at all.
question_patterns: what counts as cash and cash equivalents in a cash flow statement
why are bank overdraft and cash credit taken as cash equivalents
state the maturity window for a deposit to qualify as a cash equivalent
are marketable securities treated as cash equivalents
what does a movement between cash and equivalents mean for the statement
distinguish cash from cash equivalents with instances

solution_steps.explain: the item must be convertible into a known amount of cash quickly and without significant risk
short-term deposits and securities maturing within roughly three months qualify; longer placements are investments
bank overdrafts repayable on demand are carried as part of cash and equivalents, closing the family

concepts.title: Objectives and Benefits of a Cash Flow Statement
concepts.definition: The statement traces where the cash of an enterprise came from and where it went across the period, helping users judge the firm's capacity to generate cash, meet obligations and pay returns, beyond what profit figures alone reveal.
concepts.key_idea: Profit is an opinion on accruals; the cash flow statement shows the money that actually moved.
question_patterns: why does a company prepare a cash flow statement
what can a user judge from a cash flow statement
how does the statement help in planning short-term needs
state the benefits of studying cash movements
what does the statement show that a profit statement does not
how does cash flow information aid lenders and investors

solution_steps.explain: report inflows and outflows of cash and equivalents from operating, investing and financing activities
users assess the firm's ability to generate cash, pay debts, distribute dividends and meet obligations on time
reconciling net profit with net operating cash exposes the accrual versus cash gap

concepts.title: Classification into Operating, Investing and Financing Activities
concepts.definition: Every cash movement lands in one of three buckets: operating activities from the main revenue-producing work, investing activities from buying and selling long-term assets and investments, and financing activities from changing the equity and borrowing base.
concepts.key_idea: Classification is by the nature of the business event, not by the account title -- the same item can shift buckets between enterprises.
question_patterns: classify cash flows into operating, investing and financing activities
under which head does the purchase of machinery fall
where do proceeds from issuing shares appear in the statement
is cash received from trade receivables an operating flow
classify redemption of preference shares in the statement
how do the three activity heads join into the net change in cash

solution_steps.explain: receipts and payments of the main revenue activity -- sales collections, supplier payments, wages, taxes -- are operating
purchase and sale of fixed assets, non-current investments and the interest or dividend earned on them are investing
share issues, debentures, long-term loans, their repayments, interest and dividends paid are financing; the three totals add to the net change in cash

concepts.title: Treatment of Peculiar Items
concepts.definition: Special items follow fixed homes: income tax rides with operating flows unless tied to investing or financing, interest and dividends paid and received go to financing and investing for a non-financial enterprise (all operating for a financial one), extraordinary items are disclosed separately, and non-cash deals never enter the statement.
concepts.key_idea: Machinery bought by issuing shares changes no cash, so it is disclosed outside the statement, not inside it.
question_patterns: how are interest paid and dividend paid classified for a non-financial company
under which head does income tax paid appear
where do extraordinary cash flows go in the statement
why is machinery purchased by issuing shares left out of the statement
how does classification differ for a financial enterprise
treat capital gains tax on sale of a fixed asset in the statement

solution_steps.explain: taxes on income default to operating; capital gains tax follows the investing sale; dividend tax follows the financing payment
non-financial enterprise: interest and dividends paid under financing, received under investing; financial enterprise: all under operating except dividends paid
assets acquired through share issues and debentures redeemed by shares are disclosed in notes, never as cash flows

concepts.title: Net Profit before Tax and Extraordinary Items
concepts.definition: The indirect method starts not from the bottom-line profit but from profit before tax and extraordinary items, built by adding back the tax provision (and any financing charges like the previous year's proposed dividend) to the net profit reported.
concepts.key_idea: Tax is deducted only once -- at the very end, as the actual tax paid -- so it must first be added back to the reported profit.
question_patterns: calculate net profit before tax and extraordinary items from net profit
why does the indirect method start from profit before tax
add back the provision for taxation to the reported profit
where does proposed dividend of the previous year enter the calculation
what is the starting point of cash flows from operating activities
restate profit after tax as the pre-tax figure

solution_steps.explain: net profit after tax plus the provision for tax made in the profit statement

concepts.title: Cash Flow from Operating Activities (Indirect Method)
concepts.definition: From the pre-tax profit, add back non-cash charges and financing costs, drop non-operating incomes, then adjust for working capital movements -- rises in current assets and falls in current liabilities come off, falls in current assets and rises in current liabilities go on -- and finally deduct the tax actually paid.
concepts.formula: net_cash_from_operating_activities = profit_before_tax_and_extraordinary + non_cash_expenses - non_operating_incomes - increase_in_current_assets - decrease_in_current_liabilities + increase_in_current_liabilities - income_tax_paid
concepts.key_idea: The accrual profit walks to cash through four stops: non-cash items, non-operating items, working capital, tax paid.
question_patterns: calculate cash flow from operating activities by the indirect method
adjust net profit for depreciation and working capital changes
prepare the operating activities section of a cash flow statement
why is depreciation added back and an increase in debtors deducted
find cash generated from operations and then the net operating cash flow
how does tax paid enter the operating activities computation

solution_steps.explain: net profit after tax plus the tax provision made
add depreciation, goodwill written off and finance costs; subtract incomes like profit on sale of machinery
deduct increases in current assets and decreases in current liabilities; add decreases in current assets and increases in current liabilities
income tax paid comes off last to give net cash from operating activities

concepts.title: Income Tax Paid from the Provision Account
concepts.definition: When only provision balances and the year's charge are known, tax actually paid is found by balancing the provision for taxation account: opening provision plus the current charge minus the closing provision.
concepts.key_idea: The unpaid remainder just rolls into the closing balance; only the debited amount actually left the bank.
question_patterns: compute income tax paid from the provision for taxation account
find the tax actually paid during the year from opening and closing provisions
how much tax was deposited when only provisions are given
balance the taxation provision to derive the payment
does the provision made equal the tax paid in cash
derive the cash outflow for tax from provision data

solution_steps.explain: opening provision plus the charge made in the profit statement, less the closing provision, is what was paid

concepts.title: Cash Collected from Customers
concepts.definition: Under the direct view, cash collected from customers is the period's revenue from operations adjusted for the movement in trade receivables: open with revenue, add receivables outstanding at the start, take away those still outstanding at the end.
concepts.key_idea: Sales not yet collected sit in receivables, so growth in debtors silently holds cash back.
concepts.textbook_ref: leac206.txt section 6.6, Test your Understanding II (lines 941-1000)
question_patterns: compute cash collected from customers during the year
convert revenue from operations into cash receipts from debtors
adjust sales for opening and closing trade receivables
how much cash did the customers actually pay
does a rise in debtors reduce cash collected from sales
derive the receipt figure from revenue and receivable balances

solution_steps.explain: opening receivables join the period's revenue; closing receivables have not yet paid

concepts.title: Machinery Purchased (Balancing the Asset Account)
concepts.definition: When only balances and sale details are known, the cash spent on new machinery is the balancing figure of the machinery account: closing balance plus the cost of machines sold during the year minus the opening balance.
concepts.key_idea: Carry assets at cost, park depreciation in its own account, and the missing figure -- the purchase -- falls out of the account.
question_patterns: calculate the cost of machinery purchased during the year
find the cash spent on new machines from the asset account
balance the machinery account to get the purchase figure
how much machinery was bought when one machine was sold
derive the investing outflow on plant from opening and closing balances
what was the balancing figure in the machinery account

solution_steps.explain: closing machinery plus the cost of machines removed by sale, less opening machinery, is the year's purchase

concepts.title: Depreciation Provided (Balancing Accumulated Depreciation)
concepts.definition: The year's depreciation charge is the balancing figure of the accumulated depreciation account: closing balance plus depreciation removed with the sold asset minus opening balance.
concepts.key_idea: This recovered charge is the non-cash expense that gets added back inside operating activities.
question_patterns: calculate the depreciation provided during the year
balance the accumulated depreciation account for the charge
how much depreciation was charged when an asset was sold
find the depreciation to add back in operating activities
derive the year's charge from opening and closing accumulated depreciation
what depreciation travelled with the asset sold

solution_steps.explain: closing accumulated depreciation plus the depreciation on the asset sold, less opening, gives the year's charge

concepts.title: Borrowings Raised (Balancing the Loan Account)
concepts.definition: Fresh long-term borrowings are the balancing figure of the loan account: closing loan balance plus loans repaid during the year minus the opening balance, and the figure becomes a financing inflow.
concepts.key_idea: The account tells both sides of the financing story -- the repayment that went out and the fresh money that came in.
question_patterns: calculate the proceeds from long-term borrowings during the year
balance the loan account to find the fresh loan raised
how much was borrowed when part of the loan was repaid
find the financing inflow from movement in long-term loans
derive new borrowings from opening and closing balances and repayments
what does the balancing figure of the loan account represent

solution_steps.explain: closing balance plus repayments made, less opening balance, is the fresh money raised

concepts.title: Net Increase in Cash and Closing Balance
concepts.definition: The three activity totals -- operating, investing and financing -- add to the net increase or decrease in cash and equivalents, and adding that change to the opening balance produces the closing cash and equivalents that must tie to the balance sheet.
concepts.key_idea: The closing figure is the proof line: if it does not match the bank and cash balances, an item is misclassified or missing.
question_patterns: compute the net increase or decrease in cash for the year
add the three activity totals into one cash movement
find the closing cash and cash equivalents from the statement
how does the opening balance become the closing balance
verify the cash flow statement against the bank balances
what does a net decrease in cash reveal about the year

solution_steps.explain: operating plus investing plus financing gives the net movement
opening cash and equivalents plus the net movement is the closing balance

worked_examples.question_pattern: Net profit after tax is Rs.{net_profit_after_tax} and the provision for taxation made in the statement is Rs.{provision_for_tax_made}. State the net profit before tax and extraordinary items.

With profit before tax Rs.{profit_before_tax_and_extraordinary}, depreciation Rs.{non_cash_expenses}, current assets up Rs.{increase_in_current_assets}, payables down Rs.{decrease_in_current_liabilities}, accrued expenses up Rs.{increase_in_current_liabilities} and tax paid Rs.{income_tax_paid}, find net cash from operating activities.
Machinery at cost was Rs.{opening_machinery_at_cost} last year and Rs.{closing_machinery_at_cost} now; a machine costing Rs.{cost_of_machinery_sold} was sold. What machinery was purchased?
Long-term loans moved from Rs.{opening_long_term_loans} to Rs.{closing_long_term_loans} while Rs.{loans_repaid} were repaid. What fresh borrowing was raised?
